paper_metadata.title: A 126-W Cochlear Chip for a Totally Implantable System
paper_metadata.abstract: In this paper, a single-chip speech processor/stimulator is presented for use in a totally implanted cochlear prosthesis system. It implements a continuous interleaved sampling (CIS) strategy. By combining the speech processor and the stimulator into one mixed-signal chip, both size and power are reduced sufficiently, so as to make a totally implanted system feasible. First silicon has been validated and typically operates at 126 W (excluding cochlear stimulation currents).
